subject: Covid-19; Jury
issuer: Multnomah County Circuit Court — Presiding Judge
title: Multnomah County Circuit Court Presiding Judge Order — 2101-00000 (10); Covid-19; Jury
text:
IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE STATE OF OREGON
FOR MULTNOMAH COUNTY
In the Matter of Implementing
Chief Justice Order No. 21-035
PRESIDING JUDGE ORDER NO. 2101-00000
ORDER RE REMOTE JURY SELECTION
On July 30, 2021, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued Guidance to the
effect that local decision-makers should assess certain factors to inform the need for prevention
strategies to minimize preventable morbidity and mortality related to COVID-19, including the level of
COVID-19 transm ission, health system capacity, vaccination coverage, capacity for early detection of
increases in COVID-19 cases, and populations at risk for severe outcomes from COVID-19. While
emphasizing t hat vaccines are the most effective tool to prevent transmission of COVID-19, the CDC also
has stated that multiple interventions should be used concurrently to reduce transmission and
recommends social distancing as one such mitigating measure.
Beginning on August 13, 2021, as a result of the rapid and extensive spread of the highly
contagious Delta variant of the COVID-19 virus, Governor Brown has announced a series of measures
designed to prevent the spread of the virus and to mitigate the risk to and impacts on public health and
statewide hospital capacity. Those measures have included statewide requirements to wear protective
face coverings both indoors and outdoors, with exceptions, and a vaccination requirement for state
executive branch employees. Governor Brown has cited new modeling from the Oregon Health
Authority (OHA) and the Oregon Health and Science University projecting that, without new health and
safety interventions in place, COVID-19 hospitalizations would far exceed Oregon's health system
capacity within the next several weeks.
On August 24, 2021, Governor Brown announced that the Delta variant had created a level of
crisis not yet seen during the pandemic in Oregon, with cases of COVID-19 and hospita lizations
statewide at a record high. The variant also has significantly impacted court operations across the state.
On August 26, 2021, I issued a Presiding Judge Order (PJO) extending the "Transition Period" through
October 31, 2021. Under that PJO, the protective face covering requirement is extended until at least
November 1, 2021, and most civil jury trials will be postponed until on or after November 1, 2021. On
September 7, 2021, Chief Justice Martha Walters issued Chief Justice Order (CJO) No. 21-035, requiring
social distancing for all public areas of a court proceeding, including courtrooms.
The social distancing requirement significantly limits th is court's ability to conduct jury trials
because of the limited space available for socially distanced jurors in the court's jury assembly room.
Consistent with CJO No. 21-035, I have concluded that the best way to implement socia l distancing,
protect the public, and continue to meet the court's obligations is to require juror selection to be

conducted via remote means to the greatest extent possible. Conducting jury selection via remote
means allows the court to continue to hold jury trials while minimizing the number of people required to
appear in person in the courthouse. Minimizing the number of people summoned to appear in court for
jury duty and socially distancing those people who do appear in court in person would help minimize the
risk of spreading the virus while still allowing the court to conduct jury trials as needed. The court now
has the technological capability to conduct jury selection via remote means, thereby eliminating the
need for hundreds of people to appear in person for the j ury selection process each week.
Accordingly, it is hereby ORDERED as follows:
l. For trials in criminal and civil cases beginning on or after October 4, 2021, jurors will be
summoned to appear via remote means (currently, Web Ex) for jury selection. The court will
allow jurors who are unwilling to appear remotely or who lack the technical capability to
part icipate remotely to appear in person in the courthouse. The prospective jurors who
appear in person will participate in jury selection via remote means from a location within
the courthouse under circumstances that comply with the CJO and CDC Guidance. The
court will adopt appropriate procedures for conducting the jury selection process remotely,
including procedures for conducting trials in the event technological or other barriers
interfere with remote j ury selection.
2. Jurors selected to serve as jurors and alternate jurors for a particular trial shall be required
to appear in person for the remainder of the tria l, unless the parties have stipulated to and
the court has ordered a fu lly remote jury trial. Protective face coverings shall be required
for the trial as specified in my August 26 PJO, and social distancing shall be required for the
trial as specified in CJO 21-035.
3. Remote jury selection appl ies to j urors and prospective jurors only. Al l other participants in
the jury selection process-lawyers, parties, and the judge-shall appear in person in the
courtroom for the jury se lection process, unless the parties have stipulated to and the court
has ordered a fully remote jury trial. The trial itself will be conducted in t he courtroom in
accordance with Oregon law.
This order takes effect immediately and shall remain in effect until extended or terminated by
further order of this court.
